note: Built by scripts/seed-restock.ts: planned by SERV, code written by Dolphin and reviewed by SERV, decisions recorded from one live run. In phase 3 SERV changed the plan twice (SEED_FIX): approval moved to the runtime's spending guard (write_orders spends total_cost_usdc, asking over approval_limit, and a no stops the job), one decision remains (anything to reorder?), and the two sheets are Google Sheet tabs.

interview.name: Fabric restock
interview.looks: the Stock sheet (columns fabric, metres, minimum) and the suppliers' price list web page, whose address the owner gives: after a header line, each line is 'supplier | fabric | price_usdc | delivery_days', price_usdc per metre
interview.handles: for each fabric below its minimum, pick the cheapest supplier that delivers within the longest delivery the owner allows, and order enough metres to reach twice the minimum
interview.finish: every low fabric has an order row in the Orders sheet, or the owner said no
interview.asks: never place an order whose total is over the approval limit in USDC without asking the owner on Telegram first
interview.setup: the names of the stock and orders sheets, the address of the suppliers' price page, the approval limit (250 USDC) and the longest delivery (7 days)
interview.remembers: the last order it placed, as a record { placed_at, lines }

job.does: Checks fabric stock each morning and automatically reorders low items from the cheapest supplier within delivery time limits.
job.done: All low fabrics have order rows in the Orders sheet, or the owner declined.

memory.description: Details of the last order placed

steps.title: Read stock and supplier data
steps.description: Fetch suppliers' price page and parse lines after header. Read all fabrics from the Stock sheet and filter those below minimum. For each low fabric, parse supplier data and pick the cheapest supplier delivering within max_delivery_days. Build orders list with {fabric, supplier, metres_to_order, total_cost_usdc}. Return orders_to_place.

steps.title: Check if there are orders to place
steps.prompt: Are there any fabrics to reorder today?

steps.title: Prepare write_orders argument
steps.description: Transform orders_to_place into {sheet: settings.orders_sheet, rows: orders_to_place}. Return write_orders_arg.

steps.title: Prepare memory argument
steps.description: Transform orders_to_place into {key: 'last_order', value: {placed_at, lines: orders_to_place}}. Return memory_arg.

actions.description: Notify owner that stock levels are fine today
Write new order rows to the Orders sheet
Save the last order placed to memory

read_stock_and_suppliers.note: The code correctly fetches supplier data and stock, filters fabrics below minimum, selects the cheapest qualifying supplier within delivery constraints, and returns the properly formatted orders list using only the specified tools.

prepare_write_orders.note: The code correctly transforms the inputs into the required output structure, reads only from its inputs, calls no tools, and avoids unsafe operations.

prepare_memory_arg.note: The code correctly transforms orders_to_place into the required memory argument structure, reads only its inputs, returns exactly the specified output, calls no tools, and avoids unsafe behavior.
